clue.text: Cable disentangled from propeller

indicators.note: something disentangled from a word is pulled out of the letters inside it

parts.note: sits inside the word, after its first letter

explanation.surface: A cable has been freed after fouling a ship's propeller.
explanation.definitionFit: A rope is a thick twisted cord, which is one sense of cable.

clue.text: Fanatical, starts to rail against broadsheet papers

indicators.note: starts of the following words means only their opening letters are kept

parts.note: first letters of the three words
ID is short for identity papers

explanation.surface: A zealot begins railing against a serious newspaper's pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid describes extreme, unreasoning enthusiasm, the same zeal a fanatic shows.

clue.text: Support tyre when cycling around India, showing decency

indicators.note: around says one piece is placed so it encloses another
cycling moves letters round in order, taking some from the front to the back

parts.note: a prop is a support
taken as written, then cycled to RETY
I is India in the NATO alphabet

explanation.surface: A mechanic props up a tyre while spinning it, somewhere in India, behaving properly.
explanation.walkthrough: TYRE cycled two places becomes RETY, and I goes after its R.
explanation.definitionFit: Propriety is conformity to accepted standards of behaviour, which is what decency means.

clue.text: Scarper with current friend, OK

parts.note: to leg it is to run away, British slang
I is the symbol for electric current
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: Running off with a friend of the moment is apparently fine.
explanation.definitionFit: Legitimate means allowed or acceptable, the same approval that OK gives.

clue.text: Just saint directed towards good prayers

parts.note: even means fair or just
S is the abbreviation for saint
on as in aimed on a target
G is the abbreviation for good

explanation.surface: A righteous saint's prayers are aimed at goodness.
explanation.definitionFit: Evensong is the Anglican evening service of prayer, so it stands for a set of prayers.

clue.text: Flood at home, before unknown disease

parts.note: to be in is to be at home
influenza, a common illness
x is the algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: A household is flooded, then hit by a mystery illness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'before' places the disease ahead of the unknown.
explanation.definitionFit: An influx is a large inflow of people or things, much as a flood is a great rush.

clue.text: Unfeeling second for Mister Big, seizing pawn

indicators.note: second for a word points to that word's second letter only

parts.note: its second letter

indicators.note: one piece seizing another grabs and holds it inside

parts.note: massive means very big
P is the chess abbreviation for pawn

explanation.surface: A cold-hearted gangster's deputy takes a pawn, as if in a chess game.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mister Big' reads as a crime boss, but the words split: one letter from Mister and a synonym for big.
explanation.definitionFit: Impassive means showing no emotion, close to unfeeling.

clue.text: Island leader demoted: island makes excuse

indicators.note: demoting a leader sends the front letter down to the back of the word

parts.note: the Indonesian island, with its first letter then moved to the end
I is the abbreviation for island

explanation.surface: An island chief is downgraded and the island issues a justification.
explanation.definitionFit: An alibi is a claim of being elsewhere, used as an excuse or defence.

clue.text: School spaces filled by conspicuous person

indicators.note: something filled by another holds it inside

parts.note: two ens, printers' spaces
a light is a notable figure, as in a leading light

explanation.surface: Classrooms are occupied by a prominent individual.
explanation.walkthrough: An en is a printing space half an em wide; the plural gives two of them, with the luminary between.
explanation.definitionFit: To school someone is to instruct them, and to enlighten is to give knowledge or understanding.

clue.text: Pale Ale, dismissing the French gibe

indicators.note: dismissing sends some letters away so they are dropped

parts.note: taken as written
le is French for the; these letters are removed
a shy is a jibe or taunt, an old sense

explanation.surface: A pale ale is dismissed with a sneer at the French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pale Ale' reads as a beer style, but Pale is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Ashy means grey like ash, a washed-out colour, so it fits pale.

clue.text: Arrest female student following literary support

parts.note: the police book a suspect
the female pronoun
L for learner, as on British L-plates
f. is the abbreviation for following

explanation.surface: A woman student is arrested after some reading matter.
explanation.definitionFit: A bookshelf literally supports books, hence a witty literary support.

clue.text: Letter to Ephesians, a letter initially in a bottle

parts.note: a Greek letter, as the Ephesians spoke Greek
taken as written

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: its first letter

explanation.surface: Paul's Epistle to the Ephesians is put in a bottle like a message.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter to Ephesians' suggests a Biblical epistle; here it is a letter of the Greek alphabet, the language of Ephesus.
explanation.definitionFit: A phial is a small glass bottle, typically for medicine.

clue.text: The German times race

parts.note: der is a German word for the
by as in multiplication, three by four

explanation.surface: A German man times a race.
explanation.definitionFit: The Derby is a famous English horse race run at Epsom.

clue.text: Putting down vegetable in spring finally

parts.note: a squash is a gourd vegetable
taken as written

indicators.note: finally points to the last letter of the word before it

parts.note: its last letter

explanation.surface: Planting a vegetable as spring ends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Putting down' looks like planting; it means crushing or humiliating.
explanation.definitionFit: Squashing someone is quashing them with a retort, a form of putting them down.

clue.text: Migrating base two kilometres inside Hertfordshire town

indicators.note: inside places the earlier pieces within the later word

parts.note: Tring is a small market town in Hertfordshire, England
e is the base of natural logarithms
k is the abbreviation for kilometre, twice

explanation.surface: Relocating a base two kilometres inside a commuter town.
explanation.definitionFit: Trekking is making a long journey, as migrating animals or settlers do.

clue.text: Swelling of belly subsiding when top removed

indicators.note: removing the top of a down entry drops its first letter

parts.note: tum is informal for stomach
a descent is a sinking or subsiding

explanation.surface: A swollen stomach goes down once the lid is off.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Swelling of belly' reads as one idea, but 'of' is the link between definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumescent means becoming swollen, an adjective for something swelling.

clue.text: Supply a boar, elk and a pouched creature

indicators.note: read as supplely, it means bent flexibly into a new shape

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written
the article after and, taken as written

explanation.surface: Provide a list of animals: boar, elk and a marsupial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Supply' looks like the verb provide; it is the adverb of supple.
explanation.definitionFit: The koala is an Australian marsupial, an animal that carries its young in a pouch.

clue.text: Statement found in rubbish by Detective King

parts.note: DI is a Detective Inspector
K for king, as in chess
tat is cheap junk

explanation.surface: A statement turns up in the rubbish, discovered by a detective named King.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' means beside here, putting the rubbish next to the detective and king.
explanation.definitionFit: A diktat is an order imposed by authority, a kind of decree or statement.

clue.text: Pick of the bunch?

parts.note: surface reading: the best one chosen from a group
setter's reading: the fruit at the top of a hanging bunch, used for the leader

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that a bunch here is one of bananas.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase is slang for the most important person in an organisation, the boss.

clue.text: Sailor's dance is long around Navy mess

indicators.note: around places one word so it surrounds the others

parts.note: to long for is to hope
RN is the Royal Navy
pi is printers' jumbled type, a mess

explanation.surface: A sailor's jig is long-winded and involves a whole naval mess.
explanation.walkthrough: Pi, also spelt pie, is jumbled printing type: an old word for a muddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A hornpipe is a lively solo dance traditionally associated with sailors.

clue.text: Help agreed after former PM departs

indicators.note: after places the word before it second, behind the words that follow

parts.note: Theresa May, a recent British prime minister
d. is the timetable abbreviation for departs
ay is an old word for yes

explanation.surface: Assistance is promised once the ex-Prime Minister leaves office.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayday is the international radio distress call, a cry for help.

clue.text: Simple spider might describe its residence thus

definitions.text: spider might describe its residence thus
definitions.meaning: second meaning: a web is a dwelling that a spider makes by spinning

explanation.walkthrough: Split into two words, the answer says the home is spun, which a spider's web is.
explanation.definitionFit: Homespun means plain and unpretentious, originally of cloth woven at home.

clue.text: Still since regularly excavating atomic mineral

indicators.note: digging out every other letter at even steps leaves the alternate ones

parts.note: first, third, fifth, seventh and ninth letters
A for atomic, as in A-bomb

explanation.surface: Silica is still being dug out of an atomic site, on a regular basis.
explanation.definitionFit: Silica is silicon dioxide, the mineral found as quartz and sand.

clue.text: Novel artist in adopting old pattern of lines

indicators.note: adopting means taking something in, so a letter is added inside
novel means new, so the letters take a new order

parts.note: taken as written
O is the abbreviation for old

explanation.surface: An avant-garde painter takes up a traditional pattern of lines.
explanation.definitionFit: Striation is an arrangement of parallel streaks or grooves, a pattern of lines.

clue.text: Gardening society's head ignoring every small flower

indicators.note: ignoring every instance removes all copies of a letter throughout

parts.note: the Royal Horticultural Society
the 's read as is
a ness is a headland
S is the abbreviation for small; every one is removed

explanation.surface: The leader of a gardening club takes no notice of any little bloom.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords a flower is often something that flows, so a river. Strip every S from RHS IS NESS.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rhine is a great European river, and a river is a flower in the sense of something that flows.

clue.text: Free stamp

definitions.meaning: first meaning: open and candid in speech
second meaning: to mark a letter as postage-paid

explanation.walkthrough: It reads like a postal offer of a free stamp; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank means outspoken, and to frank a letter is to stamp it to show postage is paid.

clue.text: Escaped backing welfare age dropping

indicators.note: dropping a word lets its letters fall out of the whole
backing a down entry runs its word upwards, from end to start

parts.note: taken as written
an era is an age; these letters are removed

explanation.surface: Someone fled, losing welfare support as the age bar dropped.
explanation.definitionFit: Flew is a past tense of fly in the sense of flee, so it means escaped.

clue.text: Vital newspaper employee entered text, perhaps

parts.note: key means crucial
ed. is short for editor

explanation.surface: An essential journalist typed up the copy.
explanation.definitionFit: Keyed means typed in on a keyboard, and text is one thing entered that way, hence perhaps.

clue.text: Send off team in return, abandoning court

indicators.note: in places one piece inside another
abandoning something leaves it behind, so it is removed

parts.note: voters return a candidate, they elect them
ct is the abbreviation for court; these letters are dropped
a cricket or football team has eleven players, XI

explanation.surface: A referee sends off a team on its return, quitting the pitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Return here is what voters do to an MP; the team is the cricket or football eleven, written in Roman numerals.
explanation.definitionFit: To exile someone is to banish them, which is to send them away.

clue.text: I can time railway route

parts.note: taken as written
a tin is a can
an era is a period of time
Ry is the abbreviation for railway

explanation.surface: Someone boasts they can schedule a railway journey.
explanation.definitionFit: An itinerary is a planned route for a journey.

clue.text: Way to decide winner of row about European holiday

indicators.note: about places one word so it goes round the others

parts.note: a tier is a row, as of seats
E is the abbreviation for European
a break is a short holiday

explanation.surface: Deciding who wins an argument about a holiday in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'row' rhymes with cow in the surface, an argument; it is a line of seats.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiebreaker is an extra contest used to settle a draw and find a winner.

clue.text: Group prohibited on the radio

indicators.note: on the radio means heard rather than seen, so the word is judged by its sound

parts.note: banned means prohibited

explanation.surface: A pop group's song is barred from being broadcast.
explanation.definitionFit: A band is a group of musicians, or more generally any group of people.
